correctness.rationale: The (27-1)/2=13 complement orbits bound the period by 13. Equality forces exactly one triple from each orbit; its overlap graph is Eulerian iff its active edges form a balanced connected digraph. The 8192 complete orientations partition into 8120 unbalanced, 12 balanced/disconnected and 60 Eulerian selections. Exact directed matrix-tree cofactors and the BEST theorem give total 16*1+16*2+8*4+8*6+8*8+4*24=288 cyclic Euler tours. A logically distinct direct enumeration exhausts all 3^13=1,594,323 indexed ternary words and confirms 3744 qualifying words, 288 rotation classes and 72 size-four reverse/negation classes; output and code were replayed from the actual candidate paths. Least period thirteen follows from unique triples. The claim is finite, with fully exhaustive computation rather than an invalid extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Primary full text (Mitchell and Wild 2026) proves the tight 13-window bound and one construction, not a census or quotient by reversal and negation. The closest public span-two involution result is at shorter windows and expressly does not enumerate optima; the ternary order-three orientable-cycles result counts reversal-pair avoidance at length nine, a different property. Searches for negative-avoiding sequences, complementary three-window cycles, Eulerian orientation counts, and the exact integers 288/72 exposed no equivalent complete enumeration. Absence of a discovered publication is not proof of global novelty, and an unindexed equivalent remains a risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently worded complete enumeration may coincide with the finite 288/72 census.

value.rationale: The motivating period-sharp sequence class has a direct one-class-per-window positional encoding interpretation. Its smallest genuinely nontrivial higher-span ternary case already has 288 distinct optimal cyclic designs and 72 nonequivalent designs under its native symmetries, with a nontrivial 60-support BEST tour spectrum. An exact complete optimizer census rather than one witness is a natural discrete invariant enabling comparison and selection of optimal designs; it is neither a generic substitution nor an arbitrary unmotivated subclass. No all-length or practical performance claim is made.
